ETER

54solder joints
difficulty

A touchscreen internet radio for the kitchen table

Heat the pad and the pin together for two seconds. Feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron. Take the solder away first, then the iron.

Strip 3 mm, twist the strands, and tin the end before you solder it to a pad.

Unplug USB and disconnect any battery before you solder or change a wire. Work on a surface that does not burn, and wash your hands after handling solder.

Before you switch it on

  1. Look. Every joint is a shiny cone. No solder touches a neighbouring pad. No stray strands of wire.
  2. These must not beep. Set the multimeter to continuity and probe each pair. A beep means a short: find it before you plug in.
    VBUSGND3V3GND
  3. These must beep. Probe the two ends of every connection.
    VBUSPower in VBUS · Amplifier VIN · Controller 5V · Touchscreen VCC
    GNDPower in GND · Amplifier GND · Controller G
    GNDController G.4 · Touchscreen GND
    3V3Controller 3V3 · SD card 3V
    GNDController G.2 · SD card GND
    TFT_MOSIController 18 · Touchscreen SDI · Touchscreen T_DIN
    TFT_SCKController 17 · Touchscreen SCK · Touchscreen T_CLK
    TFT_MISOController 2 · Touchscreen T_DO
    TFT_CSController 8 · Touchscreen CS
    TFT_DCController 12 · Touchscreen DC
    TFT_BLController 10 · Touchscreen LED
    TP_CSController 15 · Touchscreen T_CS
    TP_IRQController 39 · Touchscreen T_IRQ
    TFT_RSTController RST · Touchscreen RESET
    SD_MMC_D0Controller 11 · SD card D0
    SD_MMC_CMDController 14 · SD card CMD
    SD_MMC_CLKController 13 · SD card CLK
    I2S_DOUTController 9 · Amplifier DIN
    I2S_BCLKController 3 · Amplifier BCLK
    I2S_LRCController 1 · Amplifier LRC
    amp_SPK+Amplifier SPK+ · Speaker +
    amp_SPK-Amplifier SPK- · Speaker -
  4. Plug in. Nothing gets warm, nothing smells. If something does, unplug at once and go back to step 2.
  5. Flash the bring-up test. It reports every part it can find before you load the real firmware.pio run -e bringup -t upload && pio device monitor
34ETER-WIRE-1

Eter is built

Eter is a tabletop internet radio built around the open-source ESP32-MiniWebRadio firmware: a 3.5 inch touchscreen to pick stations, a 5 cm speaker behind a printed grille, and a microSD card that holds up to 999 stations. It is for someone who wants a radio with no app and no account, and it plays from a USB-C charger.
